title: runtime-driven golden amplifier for micro-canaries
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Goal: implement a runtime-driven 'golden amplifier' that increases sensitivity of tiny micro-canaries (0.01% - 0.5% traffic) to realistic quality regressions by dynamically upweighting relevant golden prompt sets and triggering fast human-in-loop adjudication and auto-rollback when signal exceeds calibrated thresholds. This ticket focuses on the end-to-end flow: sampling, golden selection/weighting, scoring, debouncing, decision logic, console surfaces, and privacy controls.
acceptance_criteria: Micro-canary sampling can be configured per-customer+route with deterministic hashing and percentage
Golden amplifier computes a per-canine weighted score using embedding-similarity + token-level diffs
Automatic rollback triggers when weighted quality delta > 3 sigma AND at least 3 distinct golden prompts fail
Human adjudication workflow is created in Slack + Console with one-click rollback/hold actions
Dashboard shows per-canary time series, prompt-level failures, and precision/recall metrics for the gate
All stored golden records are encrypted with KMS and access audited; customer-owned golden uploads supported
design_notes:
We want to avoid increasing false positives on noisy prompts. Approach: compute two conservative scores —
(1) Sequence-level embedding similarity (cosine) against golden responses using our lightweight encoder and
(2) Token-level structural diffs (normalized edit distance + hallucination heuristics). The golden amplifier uses a
contextual weight vector: recency, route-cohort match, and prompt-provenance (customer vs. platform). Amplifier runs
inference-side (shadow path) to avoid adding latency to production requests. When micro-canary passes the threshold,
we escalate to the adjudication queue rather than immediate rollback for first-level alerts; only sustained signals trigger auto-rollback.
Privacy: customer golden uploads are stored in a per-tenant encrypted blobstore; we also support one-way hashed fingerprints for shared platform goldens.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1: Sampling + storage (2 weeks) - implement deterministic sampler, storage schema, KMS encryption.
Phase 2: Scoring + amplifier (3 weeks) - embeddings pipeline, token-diff estimator, weight synthesis.
Phase 3: Guarding logic + debounce (1.5 weeks) - thresholding, hysteresis windows, min-fail-count rules.
Phase 4: Adjudication UX + rollback (1 week) - Console view, Slack integration, one-click rollback.
Phase 5: Canary experiment & tuning (2 weeks) - run across 5 customers, tune thresholds to target <10% false-positive autopopulate rate.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Running amplifier in shadow adds GPU cost and additional KV/cache pressure; mitigate by batching and sampling.
- Stronger weighting increases detection sensitivity but risks false positives; we'll use conservative hysteresis + human-in-loop for initial rollouts.
- Storing customer golden sets increases compliance surface; require audit, RBAC and KMS and optional tenant-side fingerprinting.
- Embedding-based similarity can miss subtle semantic regressions; combine multiple metrics to improve coverage.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for sampler/hashing determinism and scorer calibration.
- Integration test: end-to-end micro-canary with synthetic golden corruption injection.
- Run a 4-week shadow on 6 routes, measure false-positive rate and Time-To-Detect.
- Security review to validate encryption/audit and TENANT isolation.
deployment_notes:
Feature gates: start behind 'golden_amp' feature flag per org. Default: off for existing customers.
Telemetry: emit canary_id, weighted_score, contributing_prompt_ids, decision_reason code. Keep PII out of telemetry by emitting prompt-fingerprints only.
